transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I’ve been eating a lot more than I mean to, mostly after work or class. I’ll sit down with my laptop and end up having a whole takeout meal, then chips and sweets and whatever snacks are in my desk drawer. It’s way more than I’d eat around other people.
When that happens, do you feel unable to stop eating once you’ve started?
Yeah. Once I start, it’s like I’m watching myself keep reaching for the next thing even though I’m thinking, Jaime, stop. I have a budget report to finish, and I’m not even enjoying it anymore.
After these eating episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit to try to undo the eating?
No, I haven’t done that.
After these eating episodes, do you ever try to make up for them by fasting, exercising a lot, or using laxatives or diet pills?
I’m not really sure what counts as trying to make up for it. I don’t think I do anything specific afterward.
After one of these eating episodes, do you ever skip your next meal on purpose?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really paid attention to whether I do that on purpose.
After you have one of these eating episodes, do you ever deliberately avoid eating for a long time afterward?
I’m not sure. I don’t think I’ve really noticed whether I go a long time without eating afterward on purpose.
During these eating episodes, do you feel out of control?

Yeah. Once I start, it feels like I’m watching myself keep reaching for the next thing, even while I’m telling myself, Jaime, stop. I have a budget report to finish, and I’m not even enjoying it anymore.
After one of these eating episodes, do you purposely fast to make up for it?
I honestly don’t know. I haven’t really kept track of whether I fast afterward to make up for it.
After you overeat like that, do you ever intentionally go without eating for a while to make up for it?
I—I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid close attention to whether I skip eating afterward on purpose.
When you eat this way, do you ever deliberately exercise hard afterward to make up for it?
I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really noticed whether I exercise harder afterward on purpose.
After these eating episodes, do you feel very guilty or disgusted with yourself?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid much attention to how I feel about myself afterward.
During these episodes, do you eat an amount of food that most people would consider unusually large for the situation?

Yeah. After work or class, I’ll sit down with my laptop and eat a whole takeout meal, then chips, sweets, and whatever snacks I have around. It’s way more than I planned to eat, or than I’d eat if anyone else were there.
After you eat this way, do you regularly do anything on purpose to keep from gaining weight?
I don’t know. I haven’t really thought about whether I do things specifically to prevent gaining weight afterward.
Do these eating episodes upset you a lot?
I’m not sure. I mean, I know it happens, but I haven’t really stopped to think about how upset it makes me afterward.
After you eat this way, do you ever do anything on purpose to try to undo it?
I’m not really sure what counts as trying to undo it. I haven’t noticed myself doing anything deliberately afterward—I mostly just feel like it already happened.
After you eat this way, do you ever intentionally take laxatives or diet pills?
I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed myself taking anything like that after I eat.
After these eating episodes, do you ever purposely fast to make up for them?
I don’t think I purposely fast afterward. I usually just go on with my day.
Do these eating episodes cause you a lot of distress?

Yeah, I think so. I’ve been avoiding plans with friends and family, especially things like cooking nights, because I’m worried they’ll notice how much I’ve been eating on my own. It’s made me pretty isolated outside of work and school.
How often do these eating episodes happen?
I looked back at my journal and my food delivery charges, and it’s been happening most weeks since the restructuring started—usually more than once a week, not just occasionally.
